numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Rolling kurtosis (roll_kurt in pandas/_libs/window/aggregations.pyx) produces polluted/incorrect values when values are large (e.g. range (-1000, 1000)): the window accumulates floating-point error from old historical values, because the running moment update is not recomputed from scratch on instability.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Rolling kurtosis should remain stable and accurate over the window; old (historical) values should not pollute the result. The fix recomputes the window from scratch on numerical instability and computes central moments online.
trigger_conditions: rolling kurt over data with large magnitude values, e.g. values in (-1000, 1000)
rolling window updated by adding and removing observations so historical values pollute later results
floating-point cancellation causing numerical instability in the running fourth-moment computation
oracle_clues: Maintainer asked whether the issue is caused by loss of precision; reporter disputed this, arguing (-1000, 1000) is not very large
Fix PR #63143 closes issue #54380 and adds tests for numerical stability of kurt and skew
Commit message: fix(roll_kurt): use online update with instability check

Test test_rolling_skew_kurt_large_value_range gained a case with data [1e6, -1e6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] and expected kurt values with window 4, referenced to GH 61416 (expected numbers not given in passages)

New test test_same_result_with_different_lengths (GH-54380) uses seeded normal data with loc=0.0, scale=1e3 and checks that skew/kurt results for a shorter series match those of a longer series with window size 8

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Values around -1000 to 1000 were reported as not very large by the reporter, while a maintainer said the values were quite large for these algorithms (issue#54380); a test uses data with a scale of 1e3 and a value of 1e6 with -1e6 for kurt/skew large-value-range checks.
category_specific_evidence: Issue #54380: a maintainer asked whether the rolling skew/kurt discrepancy was caused by loss of precision, noting the values were quite large for these algorithms; the reporter disagreed, saying (-1000, 1000) is not very large.
Issue #54380 reporter suggested the rolling algorithm should keep historical values stable as new values arrive, and a temporary fix removed the value-minus-mean code.
Test test_rolling_skew_kurt_large_value_range gained a case with data [1e6, -1e6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] and expected values for kurt with window 4, referenced to GH 61416.

New test test_same_result_with_different_lengths (GH-54380) generates normal data with loc=0.0, scale=1e3 using a seeded RNG and checks that skew/kurt results for a shorter series match those of a longer series with window size 8.
Diff in aggregations.pyx updates the online moment accumulators (m2, m3, m4 with delta_n terms) and adds a GH#42064 note about recording the number of same values to remove floating point artifacts.
Diff in aggregations.pyx references #18044, noting that with a uniform distribution floating point issues cause B != 0 and a wrong result.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction depends on the rolling skew/kurt online update path; the passages do not specify the dtype or precision (float64 vs other) in which the discrepancy appears.
The reporter and maintainer disagree on whether the cause is floating point precision loss, so a reproduction should test both the large-magnitude and moderate-magnitude regimes.
No explicit tolerance is given in the passages for separating correct from incorrect results; the test uses assert_series_equal with default tolerances, which are not stated in the passages.
